jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
Executive Director

Los Angeles, CA
About the Organization

The Anti-Recidivism Coalition (ARC) works to end mass incarceration in California. To ensure our communities are safe, healthy, and whole, ARC empowers formerly and currently incarcerated people to thrive by providing a support network, comprehensive reentry services, and opportunities to advocate for policy change. Through our grassroots policy advocacy, we are dedicated to transforming the criminal justice system so that it is more just and equitable for all people. Learn more at: www.antirecidivism.org.
Position Summary

The Executive Director will lead the Anti-Recidivism Coalition (ARC) in advancing its mission to support reentry, foster healthier communities, advocate for a fairer criminal justice system, and promote acceptance of formerly incarcerated individuals and ARC’s members. Reporting to the Board of Directors and working closely with the organization’s founder as needed, the Executive Director will oversee all of ARC’s programmatic and operational functions, facilitate its growth, and ensure its sustainability. This position is fully onsite at ARC’s headquarters in Los Angeles.
Essential Job Functions

Implement and execute ARC’s Strategic Planning processes in partnership with key staff and stakeholders, including the Board of Directors.
Oversee all operational, financial, administrative, and personnel management of the organization, with its $24M+ operating budget and staff of nearly 200.
Assess current staffing and develop an ongoing plan to further strengthen the overall team, particularly at the senior level. Manage executive leadership team as appropriate and provide overall leadership for the organization’s staff.
Ensure that a best-practices human resource department is fully functional, which includes effective hiring, recruiting, onboarding, outlining performance goals and evaluations, while continuing to foster professional development and team objectives for staff.
As a natural listener with great empathy, actively engage members both within prisons and throughout the lifecycle of reentry.
Cultivate major donors and engage the Board in fundraising efforts, while continuing to expand and develop the board to support the everchanging needs of ARC.
Lead efforts to expand fundraising capacity for ARC, working in concert with the Chief Development Officer, Development Team, Board of Directors and founder (as requested), to ensure robust comprehensive and diverse fund development inclusive of individual donors corporate and foundation relations, and government contracts.
Have the capacity and experience to develop, pilot, and launch programming to further advance the mission and impact of ARC, including partnerships and other initiatives.
Working in close alignment with the Board of Directors, Chief Financial Officer, and other key staff, oversee financial planning, reporting and budgeting, and establish policies, norms and evaluative tools to ensure accountability and consistency. In addition, prudently manage the organization's resources within those budget guidelines according to current laws, regulations and industry best practices.

Serve as the primary point of contact to the Board of Directors for ARC and ensure that the Board is kept fully informed about significant organizational developments, organizational health, and strategic direction. Prepare for and participate in Board and Board Committee meetings.
Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree required; graduate degree preferred. • Minimum five years of experience in an executive management position at a non-profit of similar size and scope.
• Understanding and knowledge of the policies related to criminal justice reform efforts.
• Dynamic, visionary, and culturally engaged leader.
• Experienced in leadership and team management.
• Proficient and proven track record in fundraising and external relations.
• Strong background in administrative and financial leadership.
• Dedicated to empowering individuals and fostering healthier communities.
• Comfortable working across diverse communities.
• Excellent communication skills with diverse stakeholders.
• Inspirational leader with fluency in articulating the organization's vision, history, and mission.

Executive Director will have the following experience and attributes:
Passion for the mission and cultural competency.
Strategic and entrepreneurial leader.
Expertise in development and fundraising.
Relationship building, collaboration and communications.
Business acumen and management expertise.
Willingness to be present in-person, on a daily basis, and for events outside of normal business hours.

Salary/Benefits

Pay rate is $200,000 to $260,000.
Multiple employer medical/dental/ vision plans with up to 100% employee coverage, 50% for dependents.
Employer funded life insurance.
401(k) matching
10 paid vacation days, 6 paid sick days.

Please note that employment is contingent upon successful background check and/or clearance. Anti-Recidivism Coalition is an Equal Opportunity Employer and will consider employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of the Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.

jobs.title: Director of Development, Upstate NY/Great Lakes Region
jobs.description:
Job Description

This role serves as a front-line fundraiser and member of the Regional Advancement Team. Primary duties include establishing and managing effective relationships with prospects and existing donors who have the capacity to make a major gift. The Director will identify, qualify, cultivate, solicit, close and steward major gift prospects located throughout Upstate New York, in Chicago, and adjacent regions. He /She will play an important role in the success of the current Campaign by continuing to build, engage, and solicit gifts from new and current donors with an emphasis on increasing annual giving and gifts of $100,000 or more. He/ she will engage alumni, parents, and donors in the life of the University and will collaborate with school and college-based colleagues to align donor interests with funding priorities. The Director is expected to make gift asks at all levels including soliciting prospects in their portfolio for a minimum annual gift of $2,500 as they build towards a major gift solicitation. The Director will also facilitate the work of the Chicago Regional Council, a core group of University ambassadors whose primary purpose is to help identify and engage key donors and prospects.

The Division of Advancement & External Affairs expresses a shared mission that is collaborative, trusted, respectful, future-focused and is aligned with the overall University. All current and new employees embrace and demonstrate dedication to promoting shared values in an inclusive work culture to propel the future of advancement operations in their everyday work.

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree a plus.
Experience in fund-raising work in higher education or equivalent is required.
A successful record of accomplishment in major gifts is necessary and experience within an academic setting is preferred.
Possession of a valid driver’s license and access to a reliable vehicle is required.

Skills and Knowledge

The ideal candidate must be highly collaborative and have a demonstrated ability to work successfully with external constituents such as alumni and parents, as well as internal constituents such as administration, fundraising colleagues, faculty and deans.
At the same time, the ability to work independently and manage competing deadlines and objectives is important.
The position requires enthusiasm, strategic thinking, exceptional communication skills, and the ability to problem solve challenging situations. Proficiency in Word, Excel, and Powerpoint, including the ability to produce presentation quality documents is required.

Responsibilities

Manage an assigned prospect/donor portfolio of approximately 80 alumni, parents, and friends to identify, qualify, cultivate, solicit and close major gifts for the University with an emphasis on gifts at the $100,000+ level. Conduct all stages of the major gift solicitation process: identify, qualify, cultivate, solicit, close and steward. Develop, implement, and drive fundraising strategies designed to maximize current giving potential for each individual prospect in the assigned portfolio as well as other prospects in the region by creating support and facilitating cooperation throughout the campus community in pursuit of the best strategy for each donor.
Discover, identify, and qualify new major gift prospects throughout this vast region. Work in collaboration with Central Giving and School/College/Unit colleagues to develop and implement fundraising strategies designed to maximize current and future giving potential for each prospect identified.
Work collaboratively with Colleges/Schools/units and central AEA offices, including Central Giving Teams, Advancement Services, Research & Prospect Systems, Alumni Engagement, Corporate and Foundation Relations, Principal Gifts, and University Communications. Develop and maintain relationships with faculty, administrators, and staff volunteers associated with specific programs relevant to assigned prospects.
Facilitate the work of the Chicago Regional Council, helping to develop alumni and parent volunteer leadership.
Report results of all major gifts efforts in the Citrus database and to the Executive Director including, but not limited to: produce meeting calendar, generate development activity reports and system contact reports; coordinate and ensure the accuracy of data entry and maintenance of regional related development records, interactions, and donor/prospect files via CITRUS in collaboration with AEA central units.

Physical Requirements

Not Applicable

Tools/Equipment

Not Applicable

Application Instructions

In addition to completing an online application, please attach a resume and cover letter.

About Syracuse University

Syracuse University is a private, international research university with distinctive academics, diversely unique offerings, and an undeniable spirit. Located in the geographic heart of New York State, with a global footprint, and over 150 years of history, Syracuse University offers a quintessential college experience.

The scope of Syracuse University is a testament to its strengths: a pioneering history dating back to 1870; a choice of more than 200 majors, 100 minors, and 200 advanced degree programs offered across the University’s 13 schools and colleges; over 15,000 undergraduates and over 6,000 graduate students; more than a quarter of a million alumni in 160 countries; and a student population from all 50 U.S. states and 123 countries. For more information, please visit http://www.syracuse.edu.

About The Syracuse Area

Syracuse is a medium-sized city situated in the geographic center of New York State approximately 250 miles northwest of New York City. The metro-area population totals approximately 500,000. The area offers a low cost of living and provides many social, cultural, and recreational options, including parks, museums, festivals, professional regional theater, and premier shopping venues. Syracuse and Central New York present a wide range of seasonal recreation and attractions ranging from water skiing and snow skiing, hiking in the Adirondacks, touring the historic sites, visiting wineries along the Finger Lakes, and biking on trails along the Erie Canal.

The University prohibits discrimination and harassment based on race, color, creed, religion, sex, gender, national origin, citizenship, ethnicity, marital status, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity and gender expression, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law to the extent prohibited by law. This nondiscrimination policy covers admissions, employment, and access to and treatment in University programs, services, and activities.

Commitment to Supporting and Hiring Veterans

Syracuse University has a long history of engaging veterans and the military-connected community through its educational programs, community outreach, and employment programs. After World War II, Syracuse University welcomed more than 10,000 returning veterans to our campus, and those veterans literally transformed Syracuse University into the national research institution it is today. The University’s contemporary commitment to veterans builds on this historical legacy, and extends to both class-leading initiatives focused on making an SU degree accessible and affordable to the post-9/11 generation of veterans, and also programs designed to position Syracuse University as the employer of choice for military veterans, members of the Guard and Reserve, and military family members.

Syracuse University fosters a welcoming learning environment where students, faculty, administrators, staff, curriculum, social activities, governance, and all aspects of campus life reflect a broad range of perspectives and experiences. The University community values the many similarities and differences among individuals and groups. At Syracuse, we are committed to preparing students to engage with and appreciate the richness of backgrounds, beliefs, and experiences that shape our society. To achieve this, we strive to cultivate a community that respects and encourages open dialogue, understanding, and mutual respect.

CBIZ is seeking a Director/Senior Director, Private Equity & Venture Capital Business Development to drive enterprise-wide growth across the private equity, venture capital, and technology and SaaS company ecosystem in the NY Metro market. This senior, market-facing role is responsible for developing and deepening relationships with private equity sponsors, venture capital firms, operating partners, portfolio company leaders, and high-growth technology companies, while ensuring awareness and sales of CBIZ’s full platform of services to support companies across the investment lifecycle.

The role is focused on selling and expanding enterprise-wide CBIZ solutions — including tax, audit, advisory, valuation, consulting, employee benefits, insurance, and other relevant offerings — to PE- and VC-backed portfolio companies and technology-enabled businesses, with an emphasis on cross-selling, coordinated pursuit leadership along-side Managing Directors and Industry Leader as well as long-term relationship development. The individual will act as a trusted advisor externally and an internal quarterback, aligning CBIZ service teams to deliver a unified, high-value client experience.

Essential Functions And Primary Duties

Private Equity, Venture Capital & Technology Coverage

Build, manage, and expand senior-level relationships with private equity firms, venture capital firms, operating partners, and investment professionals, as well as executives within PE- and VC-backed portfolio companies and technology-driven businesses.
Develop a deep understanding of investment strategies, value-creation priorities, operating models, and growth challenges across PE- and VC-backed companies, including early-stage, growth-stage, and mature technology-enabled organizations.
Translate sponsor- and investor-level relationships into repeatable portfolio company and operating company opportunities, supporting companies from formation and scale through acquisition, integration, and exit.

Portfolio Company & Operating Company Penetration

Lead a portfolio and operating-company penetration strategy that identifies where CBIZ can deliver incremental value through expanded and cross-service relationships across tax, audit, advisory, valuation, consulting, benefits, insurance, and related solutions.
Partner with internal CBIZ leaders and existing market facing resources to support companies navigating rapid growth, complex compensation structures, equity plans, M&A activity, international expansion, compliance demands, and operational scaling, particularly common in VC-backed and technology environments.
Position CBIZ as a long-term advisor supporting both investor objectives and management execution, rather than transactional, service-specific selling.

Enterprise-Wide Selling & Pursuit Leadership

Drive a OneCBIZ, team-selling approach, ensuring alignment around pursuit strategy, client messaging, value proposition, and execution across practices.
Maintain accountability for opportunity qualification, advancement, and close, while ensuring a consistent and high-quality client experience.

Regional Growth Strategy & Market Leadership

Develop and execute a NY Metro growth strategy for private equity, venture capital, and technology markets, including target sponsor prioritization, portfolio mapping, technology-sector focus areas, and coordinated go-to-market initiatives.
Build and maintain strategic relationships with venture capital firms, accelerators, incubators, law firms, lenders, investment banks, and technology-focused intermediaries that expand market access and opportunity flow.
Represent CBIZ through select thought leadership, events, and market-facing activity relevant to investors and technology-driven businesses.

Revenue Ownership & Sales Discipline

Own pipeline development, forecasting, and revenue contribution tied to PE-, VC-, and technology-focused opportunities.
Maintain disciplined use of Salesforce CRM and related sales processes to track activity, relationships, and pipeline health.
Develop and execute an annual business development plan aligned with regional and firm-wide growth priorities.

Internal Leadership & Collaboration

Influence effectively across a matrixed organization, driving accountability and momentum without formal authority.
Mentor and support business development peers and practitioners by sharing market insight, pursuit best practices, and investor- and technology-sector knowledge.
Drive measurable growth through new client wins, expanded services, and multi-service relationships across PE- and VC-backed portfolio companies and technology-driven businesses.
Build a sustainable pipeline anchored in investor relationships and operating-company penetration, not one-off transactions.
Contribute to regional and firm growth by increasing share of wallet, cross-practice collaboration, and sponsor loyalty across the NY Metro market.

Preferred Qualifications

Minimum of 10 years of experience in business development or growth leadership within professional services, with exposure to private equity, venture capital, and/or technology companies.
Proven success in enterprise or consultative selling, managing complex, multi-stakeholder relationships.
Demonstrated ability to engage credibly with investors, founders, CEOs, CFOs, and senior operators.

Resolute is looking for a sharp, driven Managing Director to lead client engagements at the intersection of financial complexity and operational urgency. This is a role for someone who moves fast, thinks precisely, and earns trust in distressed environments where clarity and credibility matter most.
You are not a consensus-builder by default. You are an independent decision-maker who can read a room, communicate with authority, and act with urgency when circumstances demand it. You hold yourself to a high standard because you understand that in this work, accuracy and accountability are not optional.

What You Will Do
Manage multiple corporate and forensic accounting engagements simultaneously across diverse industries, with strict deadlines and high-stakes outcomes
Prepare and review detailed financial models in Excel, including forensic and predictive cash flow analyses, profit and loss statements, budgeting, economic forecasting, and business valuations
Analyze accounting and financial data related to restructuring, turnaround efforts, orderly liquidations, and sale processes
Identify, secure, value, document, and liquidate assets of insolvent or defunct organizations on behalf of creditors
Develop and maintain 13-week cash flow models and proactively surface emerging challenges or opportunities
Communicate financial findings and recommendations clearly to clients, lenders, attorneys, courts, and C-level stakeholders
Facilitate conflict resolution by redirecting disputes into actionable, practical solutions
Serve as a player-coach: set the plan, assign goals, mentor the team, and remove blockers without losing sight of the larger objective
Identify and cultivate business development opportunities within the lending, legal, accounting, and restructuring communities

Who You Are
You have a high sense of urgency. When new information surfaces, you respond, you do not wait. You thrive in fast-moving, ambiguous environments and have a track record of managing complex engagements from initial analysis through resolution.
You are precise without being paralyzed. You hold a high standard for the quality of your work product because you know that in financial advisory, details matter and errors carry real consequences.
You are intellectually curious. You dig into complex businesses and distressed situations beyond the financial statements, and that curiosity is what allows you to see what others miss.
You make decisions independently. You do not need consensus to act, and you know how to bring stakeholders along after you have charted the course.

What You Bring
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Economics, Finance, or a related field; MBA or CPA preferred
5 to 10 years of professional experience in financial reporting, analytics, or a related discipline
Demonstrated proficiency in commercial credit analysis, financial modeling, collateral evaluation, and quantitative risk assessment developed through experience in asset-based lending, commercial banking, special assets, credit administration, or restructuring
Strong ability to assess borrower performance, enterprise value, collateral coverage, liquidity, cash flow, and repayment risk, with the ability to translate findings into practical recommendations
Experience advising on or supporting financial advisory, turnaround consulting, fiduciary appointments, assignments for the benefit of creditors (ABC), receiverships, bankruptcy matters, or court-supervised engagements
Exceptional communication and negotiation skills, with credibility across borrowers, lenders, legal counsel, courts, and executive stakeholders
Comfort operating under pressure, managing competing demands, and making sound decisions in distressed or transitional environments
Entrepreneurial mindset with genuine interest in contributing to the firm's growth and market presence
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and the Office Suite, including Teams; experience with QuickBooks a plus

Why Resolute
A culture built on integrity, grit, and practical problem-solving, where good ideas win regardless of where they come from
High autonomy and real ownership over your engagements from day one
A genuine mentorship culture where career growth is actively supported and celebrated
Work-life harmony: flexibility, meaningful PTO accrual, and paid holidays
Health benefits with multiple plan options. Medical, Vision, Dental

National platform with reach across 38 states and 150-plus jurisdictions, and more than $2.5 billion in assets managed

External Relations at the University of Virginia (UVA) is seeking a highly qualified candidate to join the Student and Family Philanthropy team as the Director of Development for Madison House.
Madison House serves as the student-led volunteer center for the University of Virginia, coordinating volunteers, developing student leaders, cultivating community partnerships, and promoting a lifelong commitment to service. Working alongside community partners, Madison House connects students with meaningful opportunities that support community priorities while fostering their educational and civic development.

The University of Virginia has a strong and reputable advancement community, boasting effective, results-oriented, and resourceful professionals. Our community comprises a robust advancement organization, 12 University schools, and more than 25 University-related programs. We offer a wide variety of career opportunities, as well as an outstanding environment for professional growth and development.

Position Summary

Reporting to the Managing Director of Student and Family Philanthropy, with a dotted line to the Executive Director of Madison House, the Director of Development will play a key leadership role in a growing, highly integrated, and collaborative advancement team pursuing ambitious fundraising goals. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced professional to make a valuable contribution in support of the missions of the University and Madison House.

This position is a central External Relations Development role and will work in close partnership with the Executive Director, staff, students, alumni, and volunteer leaders of Madison House. The Director of Development will serve as the primary frontline fundraiser for Madison House, with responsibility for identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major-gift prospects and donors whose philanthropy can advance Madison House's student-led public service mission and long-term priorities.

The successful candidate will be an energetic and entrepreneurial fundraising professional with a demonstrated record of securing major gifts, building meaningful relationships, and translating organizational priorities into compelling philanthropic opportunities. They will bring a strong appreciation for student leadership, public service, community engagement, and the transformational impact of Madison House on students and the communities they serve.

Responsibilities

Build and manage a portfolio of current and prospective major-gift donors, generally at the $100,000+ level, and move prospects toward giving levels that achieve annual and long-range fundraising goals for Madison House and the University.
Develop and execute individualized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies for assigned prospects, in partnership with the Managing Director of Student and Family Philanthropy, the Executive Director of Madison House, and other University leaders as appropriate.
Travel nationally to identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward alumni, parents, friends, and community partners with the capacity and interest to support Madison House.
Collaborate with Madison House leadership to identify and articulate philanthropic priorities, including support for student programs, access and participation, endowment growth, facilities or programmatic needs, and other strategic initiatives.
Build productive working relationships with Madison House staff, student leaders, alumni volunteers, and members of the Madison House Board of Directors in support of fundraising and donor engagement efforts.
Lead strategy for Madison House annual giving efforts in close partnership with UVA Annual Giving, developing coordinated solicitation plans, messaging, segmentation, and donor engagement strategies that strengthen annual support, retain and upgrade donors, and build the pipeline for future major gifts.
Partner closely with colleagues across External Relations - including Annual Giving, Prospect Research, Corporate and Foundation Relations, Gift Planning, Principal Gifts, Donor Relations, and Communications - to develop and execute coordinated fundraising strategies that strengthen Madison House's donor pipeline, advance major-gift opportunities, and identify and pursue corporate and foundation funding aligned with Madison House priorities.
Help identify opportunities to engage Madison House's broad and loyal alumni community, as well as parents, friends, foundations, corporations, and community partners, in support of the organization's mission.
Support the development and execution of fundraising strategies that advance Madison House priorities, including prospect pipelines, gift tables, volunteer engagement, donor recognition, and targeted communications.
Collaborate with Madison House staff and Advancement colleagues to ensure meaningful donor stewardship, including impact reporting, donor communications, student engagement opportunities, recognition activities, and events.
Maintain accurate and timely documentation of donor interactions, strategies, proposals, and activity in Salesforce, in accordance with University Advancement policies and standards.
Represent Madison House and the Student and Family Philanthropy team at External Relations meetings, trainings, events, and other internal and external engagement opportunities.
Other duties as assigned.

Skills And Competencies

Proven track record of managing and successfully advancing a portfolio of major-gift prospects and donors, including gifts of $100,000 or more.
Demonstrated success identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and closing major gifts through a relationship-based fundraising approach.
Ability to develop thoughtful fundraising strategies in collaboration with UVA leadership, program partners, volunteers, and colleagues across a complex advancement organization.
Strong ability to articulate Madison House's mission, student-led public service model, strategic priorities, and impact in compelling and donor-centered ways.
Demonstrated ability to build trust and productive working relationships with a broad range of stakeholders, including senior leaders, alumni, volunteers, students, donors, and colleagues.
Creative, entrepreneurial, and resourceful approach to prospect development, donor engagement, and fundraising strategy.
Strong judgment, discretion, integrity, and emotional intelligence.
Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, and presentation skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently, and contribute effectively as part of a collaborative team.
Experience using donor database and CRM systems; Salesforce experience is preferred.

Demonstrated success cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding donors and prospects.

The Division of University Advancement strives to transform lives and unlock potential through the power of philanthropy and engagement by awakening and stewarding pride and loyalty for the University of North Texas.

Established in 1890, the University of North Texas is a place where students transform their lives through education and opportunity. With more than 46,000 students from across the state, nation, and world, UNT offers 240 academic programs — many nationally and internationally recognized. A Tier One research university and designated a Hispanic- and Minority-Serving Institution, UNT has a legacy of excellence in education, music, the arts, business and social sciences, with growing strengths in science and engineering. The University Advancement Corporate and Foundation Relations Team is seeking an Executive Director to lead a foundation-forward advancement strategy focused on transformational private foundation partnerships. This role will devote the majority of its effort—approximately 80%—to identifying, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major national and regional private foundations capable of making significant philanthropic investments in UNT’s institutional priorities, research enterprise, academic programs, and student success initiatives. Provides strategic leadership and management for the Corporate and Foundation Relations team, setting priorities, metrics, and practices/processes that emphasize foundation support growth while maintaining targeted corporate engagement.

A dauntless personality with a record of setting and surpassing objectives.

Job Description

Position Overview

The Chief of Branches is a high-level executive position responsible for the strategic leadership, operational oversight, and management of the San Francisco Public Library’s Branch Library Division, which encompasses 27 neighborhood libraries and approximately 400 staff. Under the supervision of the Chief of Public Services (CPS), this role ensures optimal resource allocation, budget management, and policy implementation across all branches. A primary focus of this position is community-centric leadership—driving the development of specialized, innovative library services that meet the diverse needs of San Francisco’s unique neighborhoods by actively building coalitions with local organizations and constituencies.

The Role

As a key member of the executive leadership team, the Chief of Branches provides strategic direction and administrative management for the Branch Library Division, the system's largest division encompassing 27 neighborhood libraries and approximately 400 branch staff. Under the supervision of the Chief of Public Services (CPS), the Chief of Branches collaborates closely with the City Librarian, Chief Operating Officer (COO), and other Division Chiefs to oversee system-wide planning, policy implementation, and forward-thinking innovations.

As the Chief of Branches, this role carries full operational responsibility for managing the division’s operating budget, analyzing emerging trends, directing personnel assignments, and providing direct supervision to the Assistant Chief of Branches, a 3618 Library Technical Assistant II, and an 1840 Junior Management Assistant. About the Organization

The Anti-Recidivism Coalition (ARC) works to end mass incarceration in California. To ensure our communities are safe, healthy, and whole, ARC empowers formerly and currently incarcerated people to thrive by providing a support network, comprehensive reentry services, and opportunities to advocate for policy change. Through our grassroots policy advocacy, we are dedicated to transforming the criminal justice system so that it is more just and equitable for all people. Learn more at: www.antirecidivism.org.
Position Summary

The Executive Director will lead the Anti-Recidivism Coalition (ARC) in advancing its mission to support reentry, foster healthier communities, advocate for a fairer criminal justice system, and promote acceptance of formerly incarcerated individuals and ARC’s members. Reporting to the Board of Directors and working closely with the organization’s founder as needed, the Executive Director will oversee all of ARC’s programmatic and operational functions, facilitate its growth, and ensure its sustainability. This position is fully onsite at ARC’s headquarters in Los Angeles.
Essential Job Functions

Implement and execute ARC’s Strategic Planning processes in partnership with key staff and stakeholders, including the Board of Directors.
Oversee all operational, financial, administrative, and personnel management of the organization, with its $24M+ operating budget and staff of nearly 200.
Assess current staffing and develop an ongoing plan to further strengthen the overall team, particularly at the senior level. Manage executive leadership team as appropriate and provide overall leadership for the organization’s staff.
Ensure that a best-practices human resource department is fully functional, which includes effective hiring, recruiting, onboarding, outlining performance goals and evaluations, while continuing to foster professional development and team objectives for staff.
As a natural listener with great empathy, actively engage members both within prisons and throughout the lifecycle of reentry.
Cultivate major donors and engage the Board in fundraising efforts, while continuing to expand and develop the board to support the everchanging needs of ARC.
Lead efforts to expand fundraising capacity for ARC, working in concert with the Chief Development Officer, Development Team, Board of Directors and founder (as requested), to ensure robust comprehensive and diverse fund development inclusive of individual donors corporate and foundation relations, and government contracts.
Have the capacity and experience to develop, pilot, and launch programming to further advance the mission and impact of ARC, including partnerships and other initiatives.
Working in close alignment with the Board of Directors, Chief Financial Officer, and other key staff, oversee financial planning, reporting and budgeting, and establish policies, norms and evaluative tools to ensure accountability and consistency. In addition, prudently manage the organization's resources within those budget guidelines according to current laws, regulations and industry best practices.

Serve as the primary point of contact to the Board of Directors for ARC and ensure that the Board is kept fully informed about significant organizational developments, organizational health, and strategic direction. Prepare for and participate in Board and Board Committee meetings.
Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree required; graduate degree preferred. • Minimum five years of experience in an executive management position at a non-profit of similar size and scope.
• Understanding and knowledge of the policies related to criminal justice reform efforts.
• Dynamic, visionary, and culturally engaged leader.
• Experienced in leadership and team management.
• Proficient and proven track record in fundraising and external relations.
• Strong background in administrative and financial leadership.
• Dedicated to empowering individuals and fostering healthier communities.
• Comfortable working across diverse communities.
• Excellent communication skills with diverse stakeholders.
• Inspirational leader with fluency in articulating the organization's vision, history, and mission.

Passion for the mission and cultural competency.
Strategic and entrepreneurial leader.
Expertise in development and fundraising.
Relationship building, collaboration and communications.
Business acumen and management expertise.
Willingness to be present in-person, on a daily basis, and for events outside of normal business hours.
